requirements.text: Actionable gate fail/block findings must route to same-loop remediation rather than terminal user stop when budget and policy permit.
Gate reports must include high-signal remediation payloads with exact refs, route, retry class, and stop reasons.

rows.question: GATE-REMEDIATE-001

state_delta.current: Current system docs treat gate fail/block as a hard agency stop condition: validation-gateway records remediation but compilers/agency stop on failed or blocked gates.
state_delta.desired: Gate fail/block acts as structured loop feedback when remediation is actionable, scoped, and within budget/policy; it should not require user intervention by default.

rows.proposed_change: Reclassify actionable gate block/fail from terminal stop to same-loop remediation input. The gate still prevents promotion, but the agent may continue inside the same compiler loop to fix issues and emit a superseding compiler output/build.
rows.rationale: Gateway findings are meant to be high-signal diagnostics. If the fix is mechanical or evidence-completeness work, stopping wastes agency capacity and creates unnecessary user interrupts.

options.label: Treat every gate fail/block as a hard user stop.
Allow bypass of gate promotion, rejected because gateway remains semantic boundary.

rows.expected_outcome: Gate fail/block acts as structured loop feedback when remediation is actionable, scoped, and within budget/policy; it should not require user intervention by default.

rows.question: GATE-REMEDIATE-002

state_delta.current: Gateway diagnostics are documented as actionable, but source tooling can still surface noisy blocker summaries that do not directly drive automatic repair.
state_delta.desired: Each block/fail report contains enough high-signal low-noise remediation data for an agent to decide the next safe loop action without chat history.

rows.proposed_change: Require gate reports to include criteria, exact missing/stale/mismatched refs, affected files/paths, recommended route, retry class, and stop reason when automation must stop.
rows.rationale: Automatic remediation only works if gate output is precise and source-backed; otherwise the agent must ask the user or risk speculative edits.

options.label: Keep noisy summaries and rely on human judgment.
Hard-code remediation in agency without gate payloads.

rows.expected_outcome: Each block/fail report contains enough high-signal low-noise remediation data for an agent to decide the next safe loop action without chat history.

rows.question: GATE-REMEDIATE-003

state_delta.current: Agency stop conditions include any gate fail/block and validation/blocking health gate, so sprint/roadmap automation halts even when the remediation is routine and in-scope.
state_delta.desired: Agency retries same-loop remediation automatically up to budget and policy limits, then invokes the compiler to write a new output/build and reruns the gate.

rows.proposed_change: Add an automatic remediation cycle: gate fail/block -> parse remediation -> mark scoped leases -> fix same-loop issue -> run required linters/tests -> compile superseding build -> rerun gate. Stop only on non-actionable diagnostics, semantic ambiguity, missing approval, artifact conflict, risk escalation, destructive/publication action, dirty isolation policy, or budget/retry exhaustion.
rows.rationale: This preserves gateway as promotion boundary while using agency to close fixable gaps without manual user commands. New semantic decisions introduced mid-roadmap can run as parallel decision workstreams while only dependent tasks are fenced; unaffected tasks may continue under normal leases.

options.label: Stop all roadmap execution on any gate fail/block.
Let automation continue across decisions without dependency fences, rejected as unsafe.

rows.expected_outcome: Agency retries same-loop remediation automatically up to budget and policy limits, then invokes the compiler to write a new output/build and reruns the gate.

accepted_decisions.summary: Actionable gate fail/block feedback is same-loop remediation input, not a terminal user stop.
Gateway reports must carry high-signal, source-backed remediation data for automatic repair.
Agency may run bounded remediation cycles and compile superseding outputs before rerunning the same gate.
Mid-roadmap decisions should become parallel decision workstreams when impact can be scoped; dependent tasks are fenced, independent tasks can continue.

row_to_kb_mappings.evidence: Validation gateway and compiler docs now say fail/block prevents promotion but may keep the agent in same-loop remediation with superseding compiler output.
Gateway diagnostics and agency retry classification now require exact findings, remediation route, retry class, and stop reasons.
Agency docs now define automatic remediation sequence and mid-roadmap decision parallelization with dependency fences.

product_impact: Users should see fewer manual interruptions because routine gate feedback can be remediated automatically.
Sprint-level agency can keep independent work moving when a new decision is introduced mid-roadmap.
system_impact: Gateway findings become structured retry inputs.
Agency scheduler must classify gate fail/block as retryable or hard-stop.
Compiler loop must support superseding outputs/builds after remediation.
downstream_planning_questions: Implement gate remediation retry classification in gateway reports and agency planning.
Add/adjust tests for gate block -> remediation -> superseding build loop planning.
Model mid-roadmap decision parallelization with dependency fences in automation readiness.

assumptions: Existing agency budget fields are enough for initial retry limits unless TASK-095 finds a necessary config addition.
non_goals: Do not continue dependent implementation work while a new decision may affect it.
risks: High-risk agency behavior can overrun scope if diagnostics are noisy; mitigated by requiring stop on non-actionable diagnostics and source-backed refs.
